lines.en: 「(You’ll die if you stay like that.)」
The screen of my shuddering smartphone.
Feeling the occasional surge of seawater at my toes, I lifted the phone.
「(You were supposed to receive the Fourth Revised Version······ but something seems to have gone wrong.)」
I knew who these words came from.
The library’s librarians, inside the [Fourth Wall].
The sender was probably Nirvana.
「(This is all I can do to help. At least a part of it.)」
With a little interference, sentences spilled across the screen.
They read like summaries of scattered parts of a book.
「Here again······.」
Sentences that made it unmistakably clear whose monologue this was.
It was definitely the content of the ‘Fourth Revised Version.’
「There were too many mistakes in the third round.」
「Poseidon’s appearance was unexpected.」
「Should I have given more thought to the probability issue?」
「I should have considered the relationships between myths more carefully······.」
As always, sentences full of regret once again.
Apparently, we had failed in the fourth revision as well.
「If, back then, I had saved Lee Sookyung instead of Yoo Sangah······.」
I froze in the middle of scrolling down the screen.
Lightning flashed across it, and all the flowing sentences were erased.
I shouted urgently.
“Wait, wait! Show me again! What did that just mean?”
The sentences didn’t return.
「(Kim Dokja, ‘Fate’ cannot be changed. But—)」
「Shut your mou th Nir va na」
Tzzzzzzzt!
[Exclusive skill ‘Fourth Wall’ activates strongly!]
The [Fourth Wall]’s power, blocking Nirvana’s voice.
The sentences vanished, and my racing pulse abruptly settled.
My mind, feverish with anxiety, turned as cold as a clock ticking with precision.
I didn’t like this calm.
Unable to rage when I wanted to rage.
This feeling of being unable to grieve when I should grieve.
“Fourth Wall.”
[The ‘Fourth Wall’ looks at you.]
“Tell me honestly. Is my mother in danger?”
The [Fourth Wall] didn’t answer.
······Damn it. Sometimes, I couldn’t tell whether this fellow was on my side.
I looked up into the air.
“Biyoo.”
Appearing in a transparent body, Biyoo looked down at me with sad eyes.
I started to say something, then closed my mouth again.
[Exclusive skill ‘Fourth Wall’ wavers.]
Biyoo lowered her eyes, on the verge of tears.
All sorts of thoughts surfaced and vanished in my mind.
Part of the tangled puzzle was creaking into place.
Yoo Joonghyuk, who had returned far too soon, and the look on his face as he concealed something.
I’d felt that something was wrong.
The strange messages the constellations had sent me. The reason Yoo Joonghyuk had searched so persistently for ‘Nectar’ after returning. Perhaps all of it.
[Hey, your mother isn’t dead yet. Don’t worry.]
The voice came from behind me.
[······Tsk. I wasn’t supposed to disclose that information.]
With a small spark, a constellation I knew well emerged from the darkness.
“Dionysus.”
[Long time no see. Is this our first face-to-face meeting since the banquet?]
Dionysus strode over, shaking his left hand, which probability had burned black, and looked outside the coastal cave. There stood one of <Olympus>’ three chief gods, ruling over this entire sea.
Poseidon, god of the sea (海神).
Poseidon stood motionless, but an ominous silence lingered around him.
Like a predator waiting for an opening, his eyes quietly surveyed the ocean.
As though checking exactly where his waters began and ended.
[The 「Probability Suitability Review」 just started, so that old man can’t act recklessly, either. Still, don’t do anything rash. Uncle’s looking hard for you.]
“For someone saying that, you’re using an awful lot of True Voice right beside me.”
[It’s fine. I’m hiding this place with my power for now. He can’t hear us, can’t hear us.]
Looking closely, I saw a barrier like an overturned wineglass across the cave entrance. That was probably what concealed Dionysus and me.
Looking at Poseidon, Dionysus continued.

[Impressive, isn’t he? The majesty of one of the three chief gods······. That is a ‘Myth-grade constellation.’ A star at the very top of a lofty constellation, a height ordinary constellations couldn’t reach even in a lifetime.]
Indeed, ‘impressive’ was all I could say.
Could that ‘Poseidon’ even stop the avatar of the Outer God who had once destroyed the Demon Realm—‘Nameless Mist’?
「Where his spear reaches, there shall lie the sea’s boundary.」
Wherever Poseidon’s gaze fell became the sea. Every living thing in those waters trembled before his sublimity, prostrated itself, and begged forgiveness for wrongs it might never have committed.
Something stirred deep in my heart.
[······You really are remarkable.]
“In what way?”
[Even looking at that old man, you don’t seem truly afraid. Why?]
Of course I was afraid, too.
Enough for my legs to tremble and my head to spin.
But more than that.
「Kim Dokja was genuinely moved.」
After admiring Poseidon’s majesty for a long time, I answered.
“Because he falls short of what I imagined.”
[Imagined? Haha, you really are interesting.]
“Why are you helping me? You belong to <Olympus>.”
[Because I feel like it.]
“What happened to the others?”
Dionysus snapped his fingers, and a screen appeared.
The companions were gathered far, far up in the sky.

The companions, bound together by [Ariadne’s Thread] and hovering in the air through [Hermes Walking Method]. No one was missing. The Narrative-grade constellations Uriel and Surya were safe as well, of course.
It was a remarkably clever escape.
The sky was Zeus’ domain.
Even Poseidon couldn’t draw the sea’s boundary across the sky.
Sipping from his wineglass, Dionysus spoke.
[Relax. No one was hurt. Hermes and Ariadne were just in time to······.]
“May I hit someone once?”
I glared at Dionysus without speaking.
[Me? Why?]
“Do you really need to ask?”
Quick on the uptake, Dionysus answered promptly.
[Ah, it’s because of that incarnation. Right, I’m sorry about that. ······Hit me if you want. Just go a little easy······. You’re a constellation now, too. It’ll hurt quite a bit.]
I didn’t hit him. Instead, I asked,
“Why did it have to be Yoo Sangah-ssi?”
[······It’s complicated.]
Sitting on the edge of the coastal cave, Dionysus set down his wineglass. It took him a little longer to choose his words.
[In this worldline, the ‘three Moerae sisters’ delivered an unusual prophecy.]
“An unusual prophecy?”
Glancing at me, Dionysus replied like an orator of ancient Greece.
[Soon, the ‘end of everything’ shall come.]
“What does that mean?”

[I don’t know either. All we knew for certain was that <Olympus> wouldn’t escape it. That kept <Olympus> busy for a while. Every scenario will come to an end someday, but we needed to know exactly how that end would come.]
Dionysus continued.
[In the process, we found several singularities connected to the prophesied ‘end.’ One of them was that ‘regressor’ with you.]
“Was Yoo Sangah-ssi assigned to monitor Yoo Joonghyuk?”
[To be honest, yes.]
Anger welled up, but I held it in.
Dionysus hadn’t finished speaking yet.
[And while watching him, we learned of ‘your’ existence.]

[An incarnation who resisted Fate, hated constellations, and didn’t believe in the <Star Stream>. A being who chose no sponsor and became a constellation on his own, and whose identity not even a constellation could discern. A ‘singularity’ unlike anything we’d ever seen. After finding you, we made a decision.]
Dionysus smiled.
[To hide you, and to use you.]
Faint traces of Stories clung to his words.
Past scenes I’d thought of as ‘good luck’ flashed through my mind.
The Even Bridge that had first unfolded at Oksu Station—「Deus Ex Machina」.
And the probability that had helped me whenever I fell into danger.
[We wanted to use you as the ‘first step toward preventing destruction.’ That’s why we wanted to use that incarnation, Yoo Sangah, to help you all.]
[That’s different from what Ares said. He wanted to get rid of me.]
[The twelve divine seats are already fighting among themselves. I don’t know whether you knew.]
Dionysus slowly rose, golden aura pouring from his body. It was a magnificent Status that only the bloodline of Zeus, king of the sky, could possess.
[The current <Olympus> is a fake.]
His golden eyes gazed at me as though looking down upon a subject.
[Just as human priests created gods to establish their authority, Olympus’ gods created myths to maintain their power. False myths like <Gigantomachia> and <Heracles>······. And this is the result.]
[The constellation ‘God of Wine and Ecstasy’ looks at you.]
[I want to end this era. And create a new <Olympus>.]
[The Story ‘King of a Kingless World’ reacts.]
The Story sleeping within me was responding to his Story.
The Dionysus before me was one of the candidates to take Zeus’ place someday.
[Anyway, that was the plan······. But now that Fish Uncle’s shown up, there’s nothing we can do right now. The scenario will probably end like this.]
If the 「Probability Suitability Review」 had begun, there was a high chance this scenario would be canceled.
Participants would receive appropriate rewards according to their contributions, but this <Gigantomachia> would be rendered null and void.
Poseidon had probably overreached to achieve exactly that.
Even at the cost of his Status and his nebula’s probability, he intended to protect this <Olympus>.
“No, there’s still something we can do.”
[What?]
“I think we can overthrow <Olympus> through this scenario. In return for my help, give me some ‘Nectar.’”
[······Nectar? ······I happen to have a little.]
I snatched the Nectar from Dionysus, then dabbed a few drops onto my tongue.
[You have consumed ‘Star Relic Liquid’ for the first time!]
[The Star Relic Liquid ‘Nectar’ reacts to you!]
[<Olympus>’ probability repairs your damaged incarnation body!]
[All your stats and skill comprehension have increased slightly!]
······So this was the power of the Star Relic Liquid I’d only heard about.
To think it could boost even my stats, which averaged over 200.
As I stowed the remaining ‘Nectar’ inside my coat, Dionysus asked,
[Hey, did you forget you just went down in one blow? And you’re going to fight again?]
“Will you help?”

[Are you crazy? Even if I helped—no······ even if half the twelve divine seats helped, we couldn’t change things. Don’t you know how strong Fish Uncle is? Have you still not come to your senses? This scenario’s end is already—]
“The end of a ‘scenario’ is predetermined. Is that what you want to say?”
Briareus the giant had said it. [Fate] couldn’t be avoided.
Ares the war god had said it, too. A scenario was ultimately nothing more than the unfolding of predetermined causality.
Yes, that was right. Perhaps they were right.
“If the end is predetermined, does the ‘process’ have no meaning?”
[I suppose it has meaning. But that’s romanticism. Ultimately, it’ll only be recorded as a failed ‘Story.’]
“Are all failed Stories meaningless? Do the Stories of those who fought to the end, even knowing they would fail, have no value?”
[Constellations might like those Stories. But anyone who does that is bound to die.]
“Perhaps. But what about this? Someone sees that Story, is influenced by it, and challenges the same Story again.”
Dionysus fell silent.
“Ten times, a hundred, a thousand. If countless constellations and incarnations, influenced by that Story, came to live out the same kind of story again.”
Even if failure was predetermined, if stories accumulated of all those beings repeatedly finding the courage to face their given [Fate].
What if those attempts inspired ‘Stories’ that took up the challenge in different ways, and those Stories accumulated?
“Would the failed Story still be useless then?”
「Stage Transformation」 wasn’t absolute.
Because that myth, too, was merely something created.
Dionysus remained silent for a long time.
Ultimately, the <Star Stream>’s probability flowed toward ‘the course many beings desired.’
A story many beings wanted was bound to come true someday.
When Dionysus finally spoke, his voice was strangely impassioned.
[So you’re going to be the first? Become the first sacrifice, the torch that overthrows the scenario?]
“No.”
I smiled.
“I’ll be the last torch.”
[What?]
“Because someone has already failed countless times before me.”
I knew.
The being who had charged a hundred, a thousand times to defeat that Poseidon.
In other words······ the being charging toward Poseidon right now······.
God damn it.
Yoo Joonghyuk, charging boldly toward Poseidon’s massive form, which even Narrative-grade constellations were edging away from.
Dionysus asked,
[······Don’t tell me you’re counting on that lunatic?]
I activated [Omniscient Reader’s Viewpoint].
Yoo Joonghyuk’s thoughts flooded my mind.
「The only chance is now, while the ‘Probability Suitability Review’ is underway.」
「Poseidon is a Myth-grade constellation. There’s almost no way to subdue him through ‘Stage Transformation.’」
「This branch is probably the only useful thing I have.」
I studied the branch in Yoo Joonghyuk’s hand.
[The constellation ‘Spokesman of Justice and Wisdom’ is startled!]
It was probably a Star Relic stolen from the goddess Athena.
Though, strictly speaking, calling it a Star Relic was a bit much.
[Athena’s Olive Branch]
What made Poseidon so frightening was that, despite living so long, he had almost no ‘Stories of Defeat.’
But even he had lost exactly once—in a wager with the goddess Athena.
I remembered hearing about it from Yoo Sangah once.

—Long ago, Poseidon and Athena competed over a city. The people decided to make whichever god gave them the more useful gift their patron deity. The story goes that Poseidon struck a rock with his trident and made seawater spring out, while Athena grew an olive tree laden with fruit.
—Seawater would’ve been common······. So Athena won?

—Yes. Athena won the contest and became the patron deity, and the city was named <Athens>. Oh······ I’m sorry. I’m talking too much, aren’t I? You’re a fantasy expert, Dokja-ssi. You must have known all this already······.
Of course I hadn’t known.
I wasn’t as knowledgeable about mythology as Yoo Sangah.
But that damned Yoo Joonghyuk apparently knew the Story.
「Even the slightest damage will do. If I can just leave a scratch.」
······An [Olive Branch], huh.
Well, I supposed that counted as a Story of Defeat, too. Perhaps stabbing Poseidon with the branch could make him cough up a little seawater.
[The constellation ‘Spokesman of Justice and Wisdom’ warns that that will be nowhere near enough!]
Still, Yoo Joonghyuk’s choice wasn’t entirely incomprehensible.
If the 「Probability Suitability Review」 would forcibly end the scenario anyway, doing even a little damage to Poseidon before it ended wasn’t a bad idea.
With luck, he might even obtain a Story like 「One Who Slightly Changed the Sea’s Boundary」 or 「One Who Stood Against the Master of the Ocean」.
······Only if he was lucky, of course.
I readied myself to leap, just in case.
But Dionysus placed a hand on my shoulder.
[Don’t go. You’ll die.]
“What?”
Dionysus’ expression had hardened. And
[The ‘Probability Suitability Review’ has ended!]
[This scenario’s probability has been found to have no issues.]
I stared blankly at the system messages pouring from the air.
The constellations’ indirect messages followed in rapid succession.
[The constellation ‘Prisoner of the Golden Headband’ questions the Bureau’s judgment!]
[The constellation ‘Abyssal Black Flame Dragon’ swears!]
[Many constellations harbor suspicions about the Bureau’s judgment!]
Everyone must have been equally shocked.
It was impossible.
A Myth-grade constellation had appeared in a scenario in the sixties, and the Probability Suitability Review had found no problem?
Ruuuumble!
Poseidon’s slowly rising hand held an enormous trident.
The Star Relic ‘Triaina.’
A spear that drew the sea’s boundary, a terrifying weapon that turned everything its tip touched into the sea’s bloody foam.
“Yoo Joonghyuk!”
I shouted as I belatedly escaped the barrier, but Yoo Joonghyuk was already right in front of Poseidon.
Even Yoo Joonghyuk would die instantly if that blow struck him.
Unable to stand it, I shook Dionysus off and activated [Way of the Wind].
But Yoo Joonghyuk was too far away, and Triaina’s tip was close.

Sparks of probability flashed in the air like lightning. Their recoil naturally pushed Yoo Joonghyuk backward. The gentle fragrance of spring spread along with a black aura. Someone was blocking Poseidon’s path.
[Poseidon, why are you interfering in the children’s fight?]
Where the sparks faded, a graceful goddess stood.
A deity with half her face hidden behind a folding fan, her body wrapped in a black silk cape. Her face was unfamiliar, so I didn’t recognize her at first.
Dionysus shrieked.
[What? What’s that auntie doing there!]
A radiance that could bloom only in the darkest places underground stood before Poseidon’s spear.
[Persephone.]
As though the entire sea were enraged, a fierce sea wind shook her collar.
Persephone glanced my way and smiled.
I was grateful, but my feelings were complicated.
Why had Persephone appeared?
I’d thought <Underworld> wouldn’t intervene directly in this······.
Could it be······ to claim a share of the ‘Giant Story’?
Wouldn’t that make things terribly complicated?
[Persephone, why do you stand in my way?]
[I came to ask you to stop here. Look. This is excessive. All Your Majesty’s subjects are terrified.]

Countless creatures trembled in the waters she indicated. Aquatic species (水生種) that had turned belly-up and died merely from encountering his Status. Even giant monsters of grade two and above, including a terrified kraken, held their breath without moving.
[The constellation ‘Guardian of Pure Moonlight’ laments the deaths of innocent creatures!]
[The constellation ‘Goddess of Love and Beauty’ urges the ‘Spear that Parts the Boundaries of the Sea’ to stop.]
[The constellation ‘Mistress of the Hearth and Benevolence’ tries to stop the ‘Spear that Parts the Boundaries of the Sea.’]
Even the constellations who had remained neutral finally moved to dissuade Poseidon.
Persephone continued.
[This is no stage for a Myth-grade constellation like you. Please leave the children’s fight to the children.]
[This is no longer a matter for children.]
[No longer a matter for children?]
[My son was attacked.]
Indeed, a small arrowhead was lodged in the left arm of Theseus, through whom Poseidon had descended.
Persephone narrowed her eyes.
[Over something so trivial······. Then you need only punish whoever attacked Theseus. Have you found out who that was?]
[A giant, obviously.]
[You don’t know that.]
[I will kill all the giants.]
At his utter obstinacy, even the brave Gigantes were trembling in fear.
[Vermin who hid in the depths underground. Today, you will regret coming to the surface!]
Triaina struck down with a thud, and nearby creatures scattered into foam. But Persephone still didn’t retreat.
I was beginning to worry. Even though she was the ‘Queen of the Underworld,’ stopping a Myth-grade constellation like Poseidon was impossible.
[Move. Even if you are my younger brother’s wife, I will kill you if you do not move.]
Despite the chilling threat, Persephone didn’t retreat.
And Poseidon’s Triaina didn’t hesitate.
Light moved. Athena and Apollo, who had been observing from the air, flew in.
[You must not, Poseidon!]
[Spear that Parts the Boundaries of the Sea!]
But it was already too late.
The moment the waves surged, Poseidon’s spear was already embedded in Persephone’s heart.
But when I looked closely, it wasn’t Persephone that had taken the blow, but an enormous hand.
A hand formed from darkness of incredible density gripped the tip of Poseidon’s Triaina in a single grasp.
Crrrrunch.
A display of probability so dazzling I wondered whether I would ever see its like again in my lifetime.
I understood why the Bureau had let the scenario pass the 「Probability Suitability Review」 without objection.
Dionysus laughed with trembling lips.
[Haha······. If this goes wrong, all twelve divine seats could die today.]
An unfathomable Story of darkness unfurling in the air.
Darkness that had remained silent for ages was awakening.
[The Giant Story ‘Underworld’ looks down upon the great sea (大海).]
One of <Olympus>’ three chief gods, the ‘Father of the Rich Night.’
Hades, king of the Underworld, had descended into <Gigantomachia>.
[Poseidon. So you have finally turned a children’s fight into a fight between adults.]
Even in the original Ways of Survival, Myth-grade constellations had fought on several occasions.
But never in a Ways of Survival scenario as early as the sixties.
If I remembered correctly, when <Olympus>’ Poseidon and <Vedas>’ Shiva clashed in the seventy-fifth scenario, all of North America had been blown away.
There had also been a time when every asteroid in the vicinity was shattered······. What else had there been?
[Stop them! We have to stop them!]
Athena, the ‘Spokesman of Justice and Wisdom’; Apollo, the ‘Almighty Sun’; Hermes, the ‘Master of the Skywalk’; Dionysus, the ‘God of Wine and Ecstasy.’ And Briareus, the hundred-handed giant, too.
The next moment, the Status erupting from the two Myth-grade constellations’ clash flung every constellation away like a toy.
Kraaaaaaash!
All the Narrative-grade constellations charging in slammed into the rock walls, and Briareus lost half his remaining arms.
No one could stop the battle between the two Myth-grade constellations.
Yoo Joonghyuk, who had been nearby, was also sent flying toward us by the enormous impact. I moved quickly and caught him.
The king of the Underworld and the king of the sea.
Two Myth-grade constellations glared at each other.
Beings whose Status could shake the world with nothing more than an exchange of glances.
Poseidon spoke first.
[Hades, why have you left <Underworld>? You have no justification to intervene. Even if the scales of probability balance, you are a being who should not be here.]

Justification. When a great being like a Myth-grade constellation descended into a lower scenario, that was essential. A suitable justification that could pass the 「Probability Suitability Review」. For Poseidon, it was his son ‘Theseus.’
Then what about Hades?
[Why wouldn’t we have justification? We came to protect our heir, too.]
It was Persephone who answered.
Poseidon asked indifferently,
[Your heir? You have no children, do you?]
Poseidon was right.
Unlike Zeus and Poseidon, with their many children, Hades had none. It wasn’t because, as some traditions said, Hades and Persephone had a poor marriage.
[Of course we don’t. We have no intention of indiscriminately having children to use as pawns in war. And my husband doesn’t keep his brain in his crotch like you.]
Ignoring Poseidon’s stiffening expression, Persephone continued.
[Isn’t the very idea of having and raising children in this damned ‘world of scenarios’ strange to begin with?]
[I have no intention of attacking your twisted values. Answer my question properly. How can you have an heir when you have no children?]
A voice as cold as the deep sea.
Poseidon’s Triaina gave a harsh howl.
[If you fail to answer properly, you and your husband will perish horribly in probability’s backlash.]
Persephone smiled without a word.
Slowly turning her head, she looked our way.
The moment I met that strange gaze, pages of Ways of Survival turned in my mind. I looked down at Yoo Joonghyuk, lying unconscious.
······Could that have been it?
Several things suddenly made sense.
Come to think of it, in Ways of Survival’s 481st round, Hades had taken a great liking to Yoo Joonghyuk and said,
「“I wish to make you the heir to the King of the Underworld (冥王).”」
Thinking back, <Underworld> had been unusually kind to Yoo Joonghyuk and me—in other words, the companions of <Kim Dokja’s Company>. It was completely unlike that cold, aloof couple.
If they intended to make this round’s Yoo Joonghyuk their heir, everything made sense.

Taking Yoo Joonghyuk and me to the ‘Constellation Banquet,’ inviting me to the ‘Gourmet Association,’ granting my unreasonable requests, and even secretly letting the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint infiltrate <Tartarus>······.
Come to think of it, wasn’t I the one who’d received more benefits?
The next moment, the world’s darkness spoke to me.
[The constellation ‘Father of the Rich Night’ wishes to make you the heir to the <King of the Underworld>.]
I stared blankly in the direction the message had come from.
What did it just say?
[The constellation ‘Father of the Rich Night’ wishes to make the ‘Demon King of Salvation’ the heir to the <King of the Underworld>.]
I hadn’t misheard.
In the distance, Persephone smiled at me.
Instead of Yoo Joonghyuk, who should originally have been named <Underworld>’s heir, I had been chosen. But I didn’t understand. ······Why me?
Poseidon spoke.
[······You are mad. You would make someone without divine blood your heir?]
[Aren’t we past quibbling over outdated notions of legitimate descent?]
[Someone who has not even completed an heir’s labor······.]
[He completed the ‘labor.’]
What was Persephone talking about?
I’d completed a ‘labor’ to become their heir?
A memory suddenly surfaced.
—I will assign you a ‘labor.’ You said you'd show me an interesting story, didn't you? If you succeed, I will find the soul you want.
—Your labor is to cut off a snake's head and bring it to me.
That had certainly happened.
The test I’d undertaken to recover the soul of the 41st round’s Shin Yoosung—Biyoo.
Back then, I’d cut off Yamata no Orochi’s head and brought it back for Persephone’s ‘labor.’
And that hadn’t been a simple test, but a labor for becoming their ‘heir’?
Then just how long had this queen been······?
[Hades! Are you serious? You would make that insignificant constellation your heir?]
At Poseidon’s furious cry, Hades turned toward me.
Come to think of it, Hades had always been friendly to me, too.
Father of the Rich Night.
Strict and frightening as he seemed, he’d never once done anything to harm me.
Strangely so, considering what countless characters who visited <Underworld> had suffered in the original novel.
Persephone’s gaze deepened.
—Demon King of Salvation, you had better decide quickly
Becoming <Underworld>’s heir. It suggested that I could borrow some of <Underworld>’s probability in every scenario to come.
Beyond that, it would qualify me to succeed Hades and become the ruler of <Underworld>.
「Kim Dokja marveled.」
If I accepted the offer here, <Underworld> could formally join <Gigantomachia>. In return, they would obtain part of <Gigantomachia>’s Giant Story.
But if I refused, <Underworld> would suffer enormous losses and sink underground once more.
And their relationship with me would be severed completely.
······You really are clever, Queen of the Underworld.
<Underworld> gaining the right to participate in <Gigantomachia>.
And I would prepare to overthrow <Olympus>.
Poseidon alone would benefit if I refused.
What more was there to agonize over in that situation?
To return to Earth as quickly as possible······ to save my mother, this was the best way.
“······I will become <Underworld>’s heir. But I have one condition.”
I quickly stated my condition.
I also said that I couldn’t accept the position unless that condition was met.
And a little later.
[The constellation ‘Father of the Rich Night’ has accepted your condition!]
[The constellation ‘Demon King of Salvation’ has become <Underworld>’s heir!]
As I declared it, the <Star Stream>’s probability moved. Countless stars looked down at me. Some envied me, some admired me, and others were simply delighted.
Then the king of the Underworld spoke.
[‘Spear that Parts the Boundaries of the Sea.’]
A voice fuller than any I had ever encountered.
[We have come to protect <Underworld>’s ‘next heir.’]
A tone that inspired trust.
Enough to make me wish I really had a father like that.
[The <Star Stream> accepts the ‘justification’ presented by the ‘Father of the Rich Night.’]
[The <Star Stream> accepts that the descent of the ‘Father of the Rich Night’ has probability.]
An enormous set of scales was moving.
A set of scales larger than any I’d ever seen.
The two Myth-grade constellations stood on either side, releasing their ‘Status’ freely and destroying the entire scenario’s ecosystem.
[The <Bureau> constructs a wall of probability to prevent the scenario’s destruction!]
Tzzzzzzzt!
[Many constellations focus on the clash between the two Myth-grade constellations!]
[Many constellations shout the modifier of the ‘Spear that Parts the Boundaries of the Sea’!]
[Many constellations shout the modifier of the ‘Father of the Rich Night’!]
[The constellation ‘Prisoner of the Golden Headband’ closely observes his rivals.]
[The constellation ‘Abyssal Black Flame Dragon’ is excited by the first ‘real fight’ in a while.]
[The constellation ‘Secretive Plotter’ silently watches the situation.]
[Many constellations praise the ‘Demon King of Salvation,’ who brought about this duel!]
[You have received 700,000 coins in sponsorship.]
